title: Arm's Length Price
simple_words: ALP is the price two unrelated parties would agree on; related parties must price their deals the same way.

definitions.meaning: Price charged in a transaction between non-associated persons, in uncontrolled conditions.
The method giving the most reliable ALP for that transaction, judged on facts, comparability and data available.

key_points: Applies to an ==international transaction== between associated enterprises
Five named methods: CUP, RPM, CPM, PSM, TNMM, plus a prescribed other method
!!No ranking!! of methods: choose the most appropriate one
Income is computed on the ALP of the method chosen

rows: Price in a comparable uncontrolled deal
Resale price less normal gross margin
Cost of production plus gross mark-up
Net profit margin against a base

insight.punchline: Pick by facts, not by habit!
insight.text: CUP suits identical goods, RPM distributors, CPM manufacturers, PSM integrated deals, TNMM many other cases.

memory_trick.explanation: Cup = CUP (price), Resale = RPM, Cost = CPM (cost plus), Split = PSM (profit split), Net = TNMM (net margin).

exam_tip: In MCQs, match the fact pattern to the method: resale by distributor means RPM; profit-based on net margin means TNMM.

doubt.question: Must we try CUP first, always?
doubt.answer: No. The law gives no order. Choose the method that is most appropriate on the facts and data, and CUP is preferred only when it fits.

mistakes.wrong: CUP must be applied first, then RPM, and so on
mistakes.right: No hierarchy exists; the most appropriate method is used.
TNMM compares net profit margin; RPM and CPM use gross margin or gross mark-up.

mistakes.wrong: ALP applies to any payment between two Indian residents
mistakes.right: It applies to international transactions between associated enterprises, and to specified domestic transactions only as the law provides.

applicability: Income-tax Act, as amended by Finance Act, 2025
reviewer_note: Confirm method names and the specified domestic transaction wording against the applicable law for the June 2026 term, including any renumbering. No section numbers or thresholds used.
check_notes: Writer: Confirm method names and the specified domestic transaction wording against the applicable law for the June 2026 term, including any renumbering. No section numbers or thresholds used.

Checker 1: Doubt answer: 'and CUP is preferred only when it fits' suggests the law gives CUP a preference of its own, which clashes with 'The law gives no order'. Section 92C(1) and Rule 10C give no method any priority, CUP included. Suggested wording: 'No. Section 92C/Rule 10C give no hierarchy. Choose the most appropriate method on the facts, comparability and available data. CUP is used only where it gives the most reliable result.'
